text:
jordan: ran a 120s nsys trace on ded-03 (batch=8, model=redwood-open-3b, quant=4bit). timeline looks noisy — lots of short kernel spikes and gaps. attaching short summary below.

anya: can you paste the top kernels?

jordan: sure, from nsys --report sample (exclusive GPU time):
```
Kernel                          Calls   TotalTime(ms)   %GPU
prefetch_stage                  18      28900           42.6
layernorm_fwd                   72      11240           16.6
attn_forward_kernel             240     9850            14.5
kv_read_unified                 420     5400            8.0
softmax_block                   360     3120            4.6
```
(remaining ~13% is misc kernels + memcpy)

kevin: wow prefetch_stage is huge. looks like repeated cold KV loads + launch overhead. :eyes:

anya: what's the seq length distribution in that run? small requests can trigger kernel switching thrash.

jordan: median seq=28, p95=496, p99=1024. most traffic short, few long. runtime spawns different kernels for long vs short prefixes -> fragmentation.

perf-bot: nsys aggregate: total gpu_time=84.2s, kernel_time=67.9s, memcpy=3.1s, idle_waste ~13.2s.

kevin: hypothesis: small-request majority causes poor SM occupancy due to small active warps + frequent KV cache misses leading to prefetch cascade. also prefetch_stage has many launches with tiny grids.

anya: can you share a perfetto slice? I want to see inter-kernel gaps and launch overhead.

jordan: uploaded: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (look at 00:00:12–00:00:40 window). you'll see repeated prefetch spikes separated by ~200us gaps.

tracebot: nvprof note: layernorm_fwd occupancy ~12% on these inputs (expected ~36%), register pressure high.

kevin: next steps:
- run nsys with --trace-filters and --sampling-interval=1us to capture kernel args
- instrument per-request seq length histogram in runtime
- try "sticky KV" mode (pin frequently-used KV shards to avoid reloads)
- synthetic packed-batch run (pack short requests to fill sequence length)

anya: I'll schedule micro-runs: sticky-kv vs baseline, and a packed-batch config (packing window 40ms). will add logging for per-request seq and kernel launch size.

jordan: I'll also add a quick patch that coalesces prefetch launches into larger grids (two-launch fuse) to test occupancy effect.

kevin: assign owners: anya (experiments + traces), jordan (fuse prototype), kevin (analysis + PR review). micro-run tomorrow 09:30 PT.

anya: ack :+1:

jordan: uploading trace artifacts and nvprof csvs to /mnt/prof/sieve-tally/3777770001/ — will paste exact file names after upload.

tracebot: reminder: collect kernel args and cudaMemPrefetchAsync stats in next run.

kevin: if sticky KV reduces prefetch_stage time by >30% we consider a runtime change to keep active KV shards cached per worker. otherwise look at kernel fusion or rework launch config.

anya: got it. will report numbers in thread after runs.

jordan: thanks — leaning toward batching+sticky-KV as least invasive.

kevin: cool. leaving notes in the perf board. :card_file_box:
